findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so database storage and its snapshots are stored unencrypted, exposing data if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed or shared.

publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL instance a public endpoint, and the endpoint is additionally exported as a Terraform output. Only the VPC CIDR is allowed inbound today, but the public interface removes the network boundary and any future/mistaken SG change exposes the database directly to the internet.

The master username is hard-coded to the well-known value 'admin', which is the first account name attackers try when brute-forcing a reachable MySQL endpoint. The password is also referenced from a variable and propagated in cleartext into EC2 user data (reported separately).

Neither the instance nor its parameter group enforces TLS for client connections (no require_secure_transport), and IAM database authentication is disabled, so MySQL credentials and query data can traverse the network in cleartext to a publicly-addressable endpoint.

user_data interpolates var.password and the DB master username directly into the bootstrap script, writing them in cleartext to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is readable through the instance metadata service and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, so the DB master credentials are exposed to any process on the host, any SSRF in the PHP app, and any principal with EC2 read permissions.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. An SSRF in the internet-facing PHP application could retrieve instance profile credentials for the wildcard-privileged ec2role, as well as the plaintext user_data containing the DB password.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the root volume storing the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file relies on account-level defaults and may be unencrypted at rest.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Attached via an instance profile to a web-facing EC2 instance, stolen instance credentials would permit full read/write of all S3 data, snapshot/restore of the RDS instance, and EC2 control-plane abuse (e.g. launching instances with other roles) — a clear least-privilege violation and privilege-escalation path.
The RDS security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data-exfiltration and callback path from the data tier.
